messages:
alex: seeing tail-walk on hosted p95 around 02:47 UTC; queue depth climbing on a subset of hosts
mina: confirmed. p95 jumped from ~110ms -> ~920ms, p99 ~2.3s for ~8m window
kevin: pulled per-worker queue_depth. workers g-12..g-16 peaked ~130-150, baseline < 20
sophia: KV cache eviction/sec spiked ~7x at same time, suspect priming thrash
perfbot: alert: hosted-api.p99 > 2s at 2026-03-19T02:47:12Z
alex: no infra deploys in window. rate-limiter logs show a tenant burst (tenant-57) of tiny requests
mina: pattern: short-seq chat completions (<=16 tokens), very high QPS, tiny token count -> poor batching efficiency
kevin: that traffic profile nudges kselector to aux-kernel for tiny seqs. when coalescer piles many such requests, effective seq length rises and kselector flips to main-kernel -> kernel churn
sophia: profiling: kernel_launch_count +4x, memcpy time +3x, GPU occupancy actually dipped during churn
mina: quick metric check I ran:
```
curl -s "https://metrics/api/query?expr=queue_depth{service=\"hosted\"}&start=...&end=..." | jq .
```
shows histogram tail moving right at 02:46:50->02:55:00
kevin: kselector excerpt:
```
2026-03-19T02:46:58Z kselector: model=x1 seq_len=12 -> selected=aux-kernel (score=0.81)
2026-03-19T02:47:02Z kselector: model=x1 seq_len=12 -> selected=main-kernel (score=0.49)
```
so flips within seconds for same short seqs
sophia: KV cache trace: tenant=tenant-57 miss_rate=0.82 -> causing hotfill + aggressive LRU evictions; priming noise
alex: so likely causal chain: noisy tenant small-request burst -> coalescer grows batches -> kselector oscillates -> wrong kernel chosen some batches -> longer GPU time -> queue backlog -> p95/p99 spike
mina: mitigations: isolated tenant-57 to a separate routing pool for 5m; blocked for 5m as emergency throttle -> p95 normalized to ~140ms within ~90s
kevin: rolled kselector debounce hotfix to canary: avoid flipping kernel for same model+route within 500ms window
deploy-bot: canary rollout: kselector-debounce v1.0 at 03:05 UTC
sophia: immediate win. additional short-term: cap coalescer growth under bursty shortseq signals (min/max window tune)
mina: repro plan: synthetic load in staging simulating tenant-57 QPS waveform (steady + microbursts) and collect full kselector+kcache traces; will try variations on burst shape
kevin: added metric idea: kselector_flip_rate{model,route} and alert if > threshold for 1m
sophia: KV cache followup: add admission filter that detects noisy priming (high miss_rate + high churn) and fall back to conservative prefill behavior
alex: profiling notes: avg batch size oscillated 8 -> 64 -> 10 during incident, CPU spin time +25%, GPU kernel launches spiked which increased per-request latency
mina: action owners: mina -> staging repro + RFC for eviction tuning; kevin -> kselector debounce and flip_rate dashboard/alerts; sophia -> KV admission filter prototype + canary
kevin: I'll also add coalescer hysteresis: avoid expanding window aggressively mid-surge; prefer slow ramp + max cap for shortseq heavy routes
sophia: propose tenant-level adaptive throttles: detect sudden persistent shortseq QPS and apply soft rate-limit or isolate to pool with small-batch config
mina: starting repro now, will upload traces and open RFC by EOD
alex: good work triaging. post-incident: document runbook steps: 1) identify tenant burst via rate-limiter logs 2) check per-worker queue_depth 3) look at kselector_flip_rate 4) isolate tenant pool + throttle if needed 5) hotfix debounce/block as required
perfbot: incident-summary: hosted-api p95/p99 spike caused by noisy tenant short-seq bursts leading to kselector oscillation + KV priming thrash; mitigated via tenant isolation and kselector debounce hotfix
alex: leaving this thread open for follow-ups. will update when RFC + dashboards are ready. :thumbsup:
